subject: D9: whether a reference resolves must not depend on how many resolved before it. REGISTERED RED — both rows must keep reproducing until Step 9a, and a row clearing fails this gate.
purpose:
Resolving a reference COPIES the definition's destination and title into the node, so markdown_core_map_lookup carries a running budget — max(100000, input size) bytes summed over successful lookups (core/map.c, core/blocks.c) — and stops resolving once it is spent. Two properties die:

  uniform      200 references to one label are identical, so all 200 must resolve or none must. 100 resolve and 100 degrade to text. §2 records this as "200 refs -> 99 resolve, 101 do not"; measured here at a 1000-byte destination it is 100 and 100, because the guard admits a lookup while ref_size + r->size <= max_ref_size and 100 x 1000 is exactly the 100 KB floor. The split moves with the destination's length; that it splits at all is the defect.
  independent  `[b]: /short` then `[b]` resolves. Prefix that document with an unrelated `[a]` whose destination spends the budget and the identical `[b]` becomes Text literal="[b]". The contamination crosses labels, which is what makes this a resolution defect rather than a size limit.

DELETING THE BUDGET IS NOT THE FIX, and that is why this is pinned rather than repaired. Measured with the guard removed: `reference_expansion_bound` in packages/markdown-core/tests/runners/complexity_runner.c goes from 0.999x to 204.678x — 656 KB of input producing 134 MB of copied destinations — and D9's own witness starts resolving. The budget buys a linear output bound by breaking resolution; the two gates together state both halves, and neither may be satisfied by giving up the other.

A reference that NAMES its definition instead of copying it buys both at once, and that is Step 9a's model change. Nothing smaller reaches it: the copy is what costs the bytes, and the budget is what the copy forces.
